+package localui
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// ExemptUnitTemplate is the image's systemd template that adds an access
+// point interface to the inbound exempt set (DEV-net-f, DEV-2, CH-7). Its
+// script fails, and so fails bring-up, if the add does not take.
+const ExemptUnitTemplate = "agentos-ap-exempt@.service"
+
+// ExemptUnit names the instance of ExemptUnitTemplate for iface, escaped
+// the way systemd escapes an instance name. It refuses any name ifaceRe
+// refuses, so nothing else can reach the unit's argument.
+func ExemptUnit(iface string) (string, error) {
+	if !ifaceRe.MatchString(iface) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("localui: %q is not an interface name", iface)
+	}
+	var b strings.Builder
+	for i, r := range iface {
+		switch {
+		case r == '-', r == '.' && i == 0:
+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, `\x%02x`, r)
+		default:
+			b.WriteRune(r)
+		}
+	}
+	return strings.Replace(ExemptUnitTemplate, "@.", "@"+b.String()+".", 1), nil
+}
+
+// BringUp starts the access point only after its interface is in the
+// inbound exempt set: start runs a systemd unit and returns when it has
+// finished (systemctl start of a oneshot). If the add fails, the access
+// point is not started and the error is returned, so the box never runs an
+// access point the inbound drop would silently cut off, and never opens
+// anything else to let it through. The P2-1 loader calls this in place of
+// ap.Start.
+func BringUp(ctx context.Context, ap AccessPoint, cfg APConfig, start func(context.Context, string) error) error {
+	if err := cfg.Validate(); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	unit, err := ExemptUnit(cfg.Iface)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if err := start(ctx, unit); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("localui: %s failed, access point not started: %w", unit, err)
+	}
+	return ap.Start(ctx, cfg)
+}

+package localui
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// REQ: DEV-2, CH-7, DEV-net-f
+
+type fakeAP struct {
+	log     *[]string
+	started bool
+}
+
+func (f *fakeAP) Start(ctx context.Context, cfg APConfig) error {
+	*f.log = append(*f.log, "ap start "+cfg.Iface)
+	f.started = true
+	return nil
+}
+func (f *fakeAP) SetPassthrough(on bool, uplink string) error { return nil }
+func (f *fakeAP) Stop() error                                 { return nil }
+
+// DEV-net-f: the access point starts only after its interface is in the
+// inbound exempt set, and not at all if that fails.
+func TestBringUpExemptsTheInterfaceFirst(t *testing.T) {
+	var log []string
+	ap := &fakeAP{log: &log}
+	start := func(ctx context.Context, unit string) error {
+		log = append(log, "unit "+unit)
+		return nil
+	}
+	cfg := testAP()
+	if err := BringUp(context.Background(), ap, cfg, start); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	want := []string{"unit agentos-ap-exempt@" + cfg.Iface + ".service", "ap start " + cfg.Iface}
+	if strings.Join(log, "|") != strings.Join(want, "|") {
+		t.Fatalf("got %q, want %q", log, want)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestBringUpFailsClosed(t *testing.T) {
+	var log []string
+	ap := &fakeAP{log: &log}
+	boom := errors.New("agentos-ap-exempt: FAIL the inbound rules are not loaded")
+	err := BringUp(context.Background(), ap, testAP(), func(context.Context, string) error { return boom })
+	if !errors.Is(err, boom) || ap.started {
+		t.Fatalf("err %v, started %v: a failed add must fail bring-up before the access point starts", err, ap.started)
+	}
+	// An invalid configuration starts nothing at all.
+	bad := testAP()
+	bad.Iface = "wl;x"
+	called := false
+	err = BringUp(context.Background(), ap, bad, func(context.Context, string) error { called = true; return nil })
+	if err == nil || called || ap.started {
+		t.Fatal("an invalid interface reached the exempt unit or the access point")
+	}
+}
+
+func TestExemptUnitEscapesTheInterface(t *testing.T) {
+	for iface, want := range map[string]string{
+		"wlan0":     "agentos-ap-exempt@wlan0.service",
+		"wl-ap":     `agentos-ap-exempt@wl\x2dap.service`,
+		".ap":       `agentos-ap-exempt@\x2eap.service`,
+		"wlx_00.ap": "agentos-ap-exempt@wlx_00.ap.service",
+	} {
+		got, err := ExemptUnit(iface)
+		if err != nil || got != want {
+			t.Errorf("ExemptUnit(%q) = %q, %v; want %q", iface, got, err, want)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, bad := range []string{"", "wl;x", "a/b", "abcdefghijklmnop"} {
+		if _, err := ExemptUnit(bad); err == nil {
+			t.Errorf("ExemptUnit(%q) accepted", bad)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// The unit BringUp starts is the template the image ships.
+func TestExemptUnitIsInTheImage(t *testing.T) {
+	b, err := os.ReadFile("../../image/mkosi/mkosi.extra/usr/lib/systemd/system/" + ExemptUnitTemplate)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(string(b), "ExecStart=/usr/lib/agentos/ap-exempt %I\n") {
+		t.Fatal("the image's template does not run ap-exempt")
+	}
+}

+#!/bin/sh
+# Let the access point's interface through the inbound drop (DEV-net-f; DEV-2, CH-7).
+# agentos-inbound.service drops every connection to a box port on every interface not in the
+# agentos_inbound table's exempt set, and that drop is final, so the owner's phone on the box's
+# Wi-Fi reaches the local page only once its interface is in the set; CH-9's agentos_ap table
+# governs it from then on. Run by agentos-ap-exempt@<iface>.service at each access-point
+# bring-up, which fails if this does.
+# Only a wireless interface is added: the uplink, a USB tether or a second NIC stays dropped.
+# On any failure it says so and exits non-zero; it never loads, flushes or deletes rules, so a
+# failure leaves the drop as it was and the access point closed. The set matches by name, so a
+# recreated interface of the same name is admitted; bring-up adds it again regardless.
+# AGENTOS_SYSFS exists for tests/test_image.py and tests/test_inbound_netns.py.
+S=${AGENTOS_SYSFS:-/sys}
+fail() { echo "agentos-ap-exempt: FAIL $*; the access point stays closed"; exit 1; }
+
+[ $# -eq 1 ] || fail "usage: ap-exempt <interface>"
+i=$1
+case $i in
+'' | -* | *[!a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*) fail "\"$i\" is not an interface name" ;;
+esac
+[ ${#i} -le 15 ] || fail "\"$i\" is not an interface name"
+[ -d "$S/class/net/$i/phy80211" ] || fail "$i is not a wireless interface"
+nft list set inet agentos_inbound exempt >/dev/null || fail "the inbound rules are not loaded"
+nft add element inet agentos_inbound exempt "{ \"$i\" }" || fail "could not add $i to the inbound exempt set"
+nft get element inet agentos_inbound exempt "{ \"$i\" }" >/dev/null || fail "$i is not in the inbound exempt set"
+echo "agentos-ap-exempt: OK $i"

index 000000000..dbefc94d2
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+# The access point's interface joins the inbound exempt set (DEV-net-f; DEV-2, CH-7). The
+# access point's bring-up requires agentos-ap-exempt@<iface>.service and starts after it, so a
+# failed add fails bring-up. It requires the inbound table, so it never runs before the table is
+# loaded, and is bound to the interface: it stops when the interface goes and runs again when a
+# recreated one is brought up. Stopping it removes nothing; the drop is never opened by deletion.
+[Unit]
+Description=Let the access point %I through the inbound firewall
+Documentation=file:/usr/lib/agentos/ap-exempt
+Requires=agentos-inbound.service
+BindsTo=sys-subsystem-net-devices-%i.device
+After=agentos-inbound.service sys-subsystem-net-devices-%i.device
+
+[Service]
+Type=oneshot
+RemainAfterExit=yes
+ExecStart=/usr/lib/agentos/ap-exempt %I
+StandardOutput=journal+console
